std::fill(&C[i * N + j0], &C[i * N + j1], 0.0);\n            }\n\n            for (size_t k0 = 0; k0 < N; k0 += kTileK) {\n                const size_t k1 = std::min(k0 + kTileK, N);\n * N + j];\n            const double relError = std::abs((actual - expected) / (expected + 1e-10));\n            \n            if (relError > 1e-6) {\n                printf(\"Validation failed at Every (i, j) tile of C is\n// owned by a single thread, so no synchronization is needed.\nvoid matrixMultiply(const std::vector<double>& A, const std::vector<double>& B,\n                    std::vector<double>& C, const size_t N) {\n    const size_t numTilesI = (N + kTileI - 1) / kTileI;\n    const size_t numTilesJ = (N + kTileJ - 1) / kTileJ;\n\n    #pragma omp parallel for collapse(2) schedule(static)\n    for (size_t ti = 0; ti < numTilesI; ++ti) {\n        for (size_t tj = 0; tj < numTilesJ; ++tj) {\n            const size_t i0 = ti * kTileI;\n            const size_t i1 = std::min(i0 + kTileI, N);\n            const size_t j0 = tj * kTileJ;\n            const size_t j1 = std::min(j0 + kTileJ, N);\n\n            for (size_t i = i0; i < i1; ++i) {\n                std::fill(&C[i * N + j0], &C[i * N + j1], 0.0);\n            }\n\n            for (size_t k0 = 0; k0 < N; k0 += kTileK) {\n                const size_t k1 = std::min(k0 + kTileK, N);\n                for (size_t i = i0; i < i1; ++i) {\n                    double* const c = &C[i * N];\n                    for (size_t k = k0; k < k1; ++k) {\n                        const double a = A[i * N + k];\n                        const double* const b = &B[k * N];\n                        for (size_t j = j0; Each element is written once, so there is no shared state.\n- **`matrixMultiply`:** rewritten as cache-tiled, with tiles of 8 rows × 128 columns and a 256-wide k-panel. Each tile is owned by one thread, and tiles run in parallel. Each `C[i][j]` still accumulates over `k` in ascending order from 0.0, so the result is the same as the naive loop.\n- **CMake:** `find_package(OpenMP REQUIRED)` and link `OpenMP::OpenMP_CXX`, so OpenMP is unconditional. I turned contraction off so the arithmetic is the plain multiply-then-add that the source describes.
